59594-betty-s-virginia-christmas.title: Betty'S Virginia Christmas
59594-betty-s-virginia-christmas.creator: Molly Elliot Seawell
59594-betty-s-virginia-christmas.description: A book by Molly Elliot Seawell. It was as cold as Christmas, and Christmas Eve it was. A thin crust of snow lay over the level landscape of lower Virginia, and the declining sun cast a lovely rose-red light upon the silver world. Afar off lay the river that led to the great bay, both river and bay frozen hard and fast as steel. The crystal air was sharp and still, and in the opaline sky a little crescent moon smiled at the sparkling stars.

70844-twilight-sleep.title: Twilight Sleep
70844-twilight-sleep.creator: Edith Wharton
70844-twilight-sleep.description: A book by Edith Wharton. "But look at her list--just for this morning!" the secretary continued, handing over a tall morocco-framed tablet, on which was inscribed, in the colourless secretarial hand: "7.30 Mental uplift. 8.30 Silent Meditation. Man with Persian miniatures. 9.45 Eurythmic exercises. 10.30 Receive Mothers' Day deputation. 11.30 Birth Control committee at Mrs.----"

arxiv-1810-02044.title: Convergence of a Solution Algorithm in Indefinite Quadratic Programming The authors were supported respectively by the Faculty of Information Technology of Hanoi University of Industry, the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) grant funded by the Korea government (MEST) No.2015R1A3A2031159, a
arxiv-1810-02044.creator: T.H. Cuong, Y. Lim, N.D. Yen
arxiv-1810-02044.description:
A 2018 arXiv research paper by T.H. Cuong, Y. Lim, N.D. Yen. It is proved that, for an indefinite quadratic programming problem under linear constraints, any iterative sequence generated by the
Proximal DC decomposition algorithm

R
-linearly converges to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker point, provided that the problem has a solution. Another major result of this paper says that DCA sequences generated by the algorithm converge to a locally unique solution of the problem if the initial points are taken from a suitably-chosen neighborhood of it.

arxiv-2109-10944.title: Measurement-Induced Phase Transitions in Sparse Nonlocal Scramblers
arxiv-2109-10944.creator: Tomohiro Hashizume, Gregory Bentsen, Andrew J. Daley
arxiv-2109-10944.description: Abstract Measurement-induced phase transitions arise due to a competition between the scrambling of quantum information in a many-body system and local measurements. In this work we investigate these transitions in different classes of fast scramblers, systems that scramble quantum information as quickly as is conjectured to be possible – on a timescale proportional to the logarithm of the system size.

arxiv-2202-03139.title: Free boson realization of the Dunkl intertwining operator in one dimension
arxiv-2202-03139.creator: Luc Vinet, Alexei Zhedanov, [.5em] Centre de Recherches Mathématiques, Université de Montréal P.O. Box 6128, Centre-ville Station, Montréal (Québec),, [.9em] School of Mathematics, Renmin University of China, Beijing, 100872, China
arxiv-2202-03139.description: Abstract The operator that intertwines between the ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} - Dunkl operator and the derivative is shown to have a realization in terms of the oscillator operators in one dimension. This observation rests on the fact that the Dunkl intertwining operator maps the Hermite polynomials on the generalized Hermite polynomials.

arxiv-2204-06343.title: Single-grasp Deformable Object Discrimination: the Effect of Gripper Morphology, Sensing Modalities, and Action Parameters
arxiv-2204-06343.creator: Michal Pliska, Shubhan Patni, Michal Mares, Pavel Stoudek, Zdenek Straka, Karla Stepanova, and Matej Hoffmann
arxiv-2204-06343.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Michal Pliska, Shubhan Patni, Michal Mares, Pavel Stoudek, Zdenek Straka, Karla Stepanova, and Matej Hoffmann. In haptic object discrimination, the effect of gripper embodiment, action parameters, and sensory channels has not been systematically studied. We used two anthropomorphic hands and two 2-finger grippers to grasp two sets of deformable objects.

arxiv-2205-09822.title: Regularisation and separation for evolving surface Cahn-Hilliard equations
arxiv-2205-09822.creator: Diogo Caetano, Charles M. Elliott, Maurizio Grasselli, Andrea Poiatti
arxiv-2205-09822.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Diogo Caetano, Charles M. Elliott, Maurizio Grasselli, Andrea Poiatti. We consider the Cahn-Hilliard equation with constant mobility and logarithmic potential on a two-dimensional evolving closed surface embedded in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} , as well as a related weighted model. The well-posedness of weak solutions for the corresponding initial value problems on a given time interval [ 0 , T ] [0,T] have already been established by the first two authors. Here we first prove some regularisation properties of weak solutions in finite time.

arxiv-2407-12282.title: Chip Placement with Diffusion Models
arxiv-2407-12282.creator: Vint Lee, Minh Nguyen, Leena Elzeiny, Chun Deng, Pieter Abbeel, John Wawrzynek
arxiv-2407-12282.description: Abstract Macro placement is a vital step in digital circuit design that defines the physical location of large collections of components, known as macros, on a 2D chip. Because key performance metrics of the chip are determined by the placement, optimizing it is crucial.

arxiv-2409-08988.title: Assembly of Complex Colloidal Systems Using DNA
arxiv-2409-08988.creator: William M. Jacobs, W. Benjamin Rogers
arxiv-2409-08988.description: Abstract Nearly thirty years after its inception, the field of DNA-programmed colloidal self-assembly has begun to realize its initial promise. In this review, we summarize recent developments in designing effective interactions and understanding the dynamic self-assembly pathways of DNA-coated nanoparticles and microparticles, as well as how these advances have propelled tremendous progress in crystal engineering.

arxiv-2412-11850.title: Causal Invariance Learning via Efficient Nonconvex Optimization
arxiv-2412-11850.creator: Zhenyu Wang, Yifan Hu, Peter Bühlmann, Zijian Guo
arxiv-2412-11850.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhenyu Wang, Yifan Hu, Peter Bühlmann, Zijian Guo. Identifying the causal relationship among variables from observational data is an important yet challenging task. This work focuses on identifying the direct causes of an outcome and estimating their magnitude, i.e., learning the causal outcome model. Data from multiple environments provide valuable opportunities to uncover causality by exploiting the invariance principle that the causal outcome model holds across heterogeneous environments.

arxiv-2503-00723.title: Re-Imagining Multimodal Instruction Tuning: A Representation View
arxiv-2503-00723.creator: Yiyang Liu James Chenhao Liang Ruixiang Tang Yugyung Lee Majid Rabbani Sohail Dianat Raghuveer Rao Lifu Huang Dongfang Liu Qifan Wang Cheng Han
arxiv-2503-00723.description: Abstract Multimodal instruction tuning has proven to be an effective strategy for achieving zero-shot generalization by fine-tuning pre-trained Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) with instruction-following data. However, as the scale of LMMs continues to grow, fully fine-tuning these models has become highly parameter-intensive.

arxiv-2602-08655.title: From Robotics to Sepsis Treatment: Offline RL via Geometric Pessimism
arxiv-2602-08655.creator: Sarthak Wanjari
arxiv-2602-08655.description: Abstract Offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) promises the recovery of optimal policies from static datasets, yet it remains susceptible to the overestimation of out-of-distribution (OOD) actions, particularly in fractured and sparse data manifolds. Current solutions necessitate a trade-off between computational efficiency and performance.

arxiv-2606-07962.title: ChronoPhyBench: Do MLLMs Truly Understand the World or Merely Exploit Language Priors?
arxiv-2606-07962.creator: Bin Zhu, Yanhao Jia, Kexin Zhao, Jie Wang, Munan Ning, Hao Li, Yuwei Niu, Tanqing Sun, Huangchong Yan, Mingjun Pan, Xinyi Wu, Qishen Yin, Yunyang Ge, Shuai Zhao, Li Yuan

pmc-10552255.title: Health status of aged women with or without the experience of practicing yoga
pmc-10552255.creator: Sarah Suet Shan Wong, Tai Wa Liu, Shamay Sheung Mei Ng
pmc-10552255.description: BackgroundYoga is a popular training practice that enhances women’s physical activity level and modifies the major risk factors contributing to noncommunicable diseases. This study aimed to compare general health and cardiovascular health, musculoskeletal health, psychological health, and health-related quality of life between aged women with and without long-term yoga practice.

pmc-10735474.title: LINGUISTIC PROFILES OF PARAGRAPH RECALL PREDICT DEPRESSION IN OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10735474.creator: Seho Park, Nicole Roth, Paola Sebastiani, Stephanie Cosentino, Stacy Andersen
pmc-10735474.description: Our previous work identified linguistic markers from paragraph recall that predicted cognitive impairment. However, many features were related to psychological constructs, and mood disorders, such as depression, are also associated with cognitive impairment. Therefore, we aimed to identify linguistic markers that are associated with depression and examine their overlap with those for cognitive impairment.

pmc-10736387.title: NOT ALL CREATED EQUAL: THE IMPACTS OF POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, AND PARTNER RELATIONSHIPS ON COGNITION IN LATELIFE
pmc-10736387.creator: Nicole Ee, Fiona Matthews, Ruth Peters, Kaarin Anstey
pmc-10736387.description: BackgroundSocial engagement has been linked to higher cognitive function in later life and it is a well evidenced protective factor against dementia and cognitive decline. However, far less is understood about how the type, quality and quantity of social engagement differentially affects cognitive health outcomes in older adults.MethodsThe sample consisted of 1972 participants aged 68-74 (M = 70.

pmc-10946904.title: Artificial intelligence in medicine: has the time come to hang up the stethoscope?
pmc-10946904.creator: David Lyell, Farah Magrabi
pmc-10946904.description: The question of whether the time has come to hang up the stethoscope is bound up in the promises of artificial intelligence (AI), promises that have so far proven difficult to deliver, perhaps because of the mismatch between the technical capability of AI and its use in real‐world clinical settings.

pmc-11334443.title: “I will take part in the revolution with our people”: a qualitative study of healthcare workers’ experiences of violence and resistance after the 2021 Myanmar coup d’etat
pmc-11334443.creator: Rohini J Haar, Katerina Crawford, Larissa Fast, Than Htut Win, Leonard Rubenstein, Karl Blanchet, Louis Lillywhite, Nicholus Tint-Zaw, Myo-Myo Mon
pmc-11334443.description: BackgroundIn Myanmar, ongoing conflict since the 2021 military coup d’etat has been characterized by targeted violence against health workers (HWs), particularly those participating in the pro-democracy movement. Existing knowledge about the challenges faced by health workers in Myanmar is scant, including their perspectives on mitigating their suffering and the broader impact on community health.

pmc-11488131.title: Anti-dopamine receptor 2 antibody encephalitis in adults: a case report
pmc-11488131.creator: Xiaoke Wu, Mengmeng Shi, Haifeng Zhang
pmc-11488131.description: BackgroundAnti-dopamine receptor 2 (D2R) antibody encephalitis (D2R encephalitis) is a subtype of autoimmune encephalitis (AE). Lesions in affected patients primarily involve the basal ganglia, resulting in a range of psychiatric and movement disorders. A majority of cases reported to date have impacted children or adolescents, whereas we here describe a case of adult-onset D2R encephalitis.

pmc-11626371.title: Krill oil supplementation improves transepidermal water loss, hydration and elasticity of the skin in healthy adults: Results from two randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled, dose‐finding pilot studies
pmc-11626371.creator: Katina Handeland, Mike Wakeman, Lena Burri
pmc-11626371.description: BackgroundDietary marine omega‐3 fatty acids and phospholipids have individually shown favorable effects on skin barrier function. Krill oil offers a combination of omega‐3 in phospholipid form which might enhance the efficacy in supporting skin health.AimsThe aim was to investigate the impact of two different doses of krill oil on skin transepidermal water loss (TEWL) in healthy adults.

pmc-12551061.title: Incidence and Survival of IDH-Wildtype Glioblastoma and IDH-Mutant Astrocytoma by Treatment and Sex: A Regional Study in Spain (2011–2021)
pmc-12551061.creator: J. A. Encarnación, C. Manso, M. Royo-Villanova, P. Ruiz, M. I. De la Fuente, E. Cárdenas, S. Ros, J. L. Alonso-Romero
pmc-12551061.description: Background: The incidence and prognosis of high-grade gliomas differ according to histopathological and molecular features. The WHO 2021 CNS classification emphasized IDH status, but historical cohorts often lacked systematic molecular profiling. Methods: We conducted a retrospective population-based study including adult patients diagnosed with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma or IDH-mutant astrocytoma in a Spanish tertiary center (2011–2021).

pmc-12714510.title: Mitral Annular Subvalvular Aneurysm With Leaflet Perforation and Left Atrium–to–Left Ventricle Fistulous Communication
pmc-12714510.creator: Daniela Harsanyi, Ana Carolina Loayza Benchimol Barbosa, Jessica Silva Nicolau, José Roberto de Oliveira Silva Filho, Léa Maria Macruz Ferreira Demarchi, Antonio de Santis, Elinthon Tavares Veronese, Carlos Manuel de Almeida Brandão, Flávio Tarasoutchi, Paulo Rogério Soares, Thiago Luis Scudeler
pmc-12714510.description: BackgroundMitral annular subvalvular aneurysm (MASA) is a rare cardiac condition with variable etiology and potentially life-threatening complications.Case SummaryA 35-year-old previously healthy man of African descent presented with progressive dyspnea and weight loss. Multimodality imaging revealed a posterior MASA complicated by leaflet perforation, left atrium–to–left ventricle fistula, and severe mitral regurgitation.

pmc-12928689.title: Leveraging AI to Advance Age-Friendly Care in the Veterans Health Administration
pmc-12928689.creator: Elizabeth Fine Smilovich, Megha Kalsy, Kimberly Wozneak, Quratulain Syed, Laurence M Solberg
pmc-12928689.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The aging population presents a pressing challenge for health care systems, necessitating effective strategies to address the complex needs of older adults. The Veterans Health Administration in the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the largest integrated health care system in the United States, has embraced the Age-Friendly Health Systems (AFHS) initiative from the Institute for Healthcare Improvement to ensure safe and high-quality care for older veterans.

pmc-13075498.title: Implementation and Outcomes of a Standardized Multidisciplinary Treatment Outpatient Model in Two Pediatric Tertiary Hospitals
pmc-13075498.creator: Miao Wang, Chengjie Ye, Xuan Gao, Yuping Qian, Tianxing Feng, Yu Shi
pmc-13075498.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). pmc-13312531.creator: Yunfeng Zheng, Shuo Zhang, Xu-Lin Chen, Xianwen Wang

pmc-13462212.creator: Tuulia Enbom, Leena Seppä-Lassila, Päivi J. Rajala-Schultz, Kristiina Sarjokari, Jenni Suolaniemi, Helena Rautala, Olli Ruoho, Sinikka Pelkonen, Tiina Autio

pmc-13471649.title: Life-course body size trajectories and the progression of cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity: a prospective UK biobank study
pmc-13471649.creator: Jingjing Lang, Zhongyang Guan, Lili Li, Lu Jiang, Guanghui Mao, Guochong Chen, Mario Siervo, Xiaoyan Shi
pmc-13471649.description: BackgroundThe influence of life-course body size on the progression of cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity (CRMM) is insufficiently understood.MethodsWe included 398,491 UK Biobank participants. Childhood-to-adulthood body size trajectories were defined using recalled childhood somatotype and adult body mass index (BMI). Multi-state models evaluated transition-specific hazards, state-occupation probabilities, and expected length of stay (ELOS) across body size trajectories.

pmc-13482566.title: A machine learning framework for predictive interpretation of variants of uncertain significance in hereditary cancer
pmc-13482566.creator: Nayeema Nizamuddin, Soham Biswas, Akshaykumar Zawar, Poonam Deshpande, Layal Yasin, Prashanth N. Suravajhala
pmc-13482566.description: IntroductionVariant interpretation remains a major bottleneck in clinical genomics, with variants of uncertain significance (VUS) representing a critical unresolved challenge due to insufficient evidence for definitive classification. Existing in silico tools exhibit variable and often inconsistent performance complicating clinical decision-making, particularly in the context of hereditary cancer genomics.

pmc-13585234.title: A systematic review of ultrasound to predict severe disease in patients with dengue and other viral infections associated with hemorrhagic fevers
pmc-13585234.creator: Daniel Z. Hodson, Renato A. Tambelli, Mahathar A. Wahab, Claudia Wallrauch, Hans-Michael Steffen, Benno Kreuels, Sabine Bélard, Tom Heller
pmc-13585234.description: BackgroundViral infections associated with hemorrhagic fevers (VaHFs) cause millions of cases each year across a broad geography with severity ranging from asymptomatic cases to clinical disease with a high case fatality rate. Commonalities in pathophysiology across VaHFs include vascular damage and plasma leakage with the possibility of hemorrhage, organ failure, shock, and death.

pmc-13679526.title: Nanoparticle-Mediated Brain-Targeted Drug Delivery for Methamphetamine Use Disorder: Advances, Challenges and Translational Perspectives
pmc-13679526.creator: Xinjie Zhang, Ruike Xu, Min Wang, Yan Du, Miao Zhang, Lihua Li, Genmeng Yang, Shijun Hong
pmc-13679526.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Methamphetamine use disorder (MUD) poses a significant global health challenge, lacking FDA-approved pharmacotherapies. Despite extensive exploration of therapeutic targets and interventions, effective treatment remains scarce due to challenges in delivering therapeutic agents to relevant brain regions at effective concentrations. Nanoparticle-mediated delivery offers a promising approach for transporting various therapeutic cargos to the central nervous system, including small molecules, nucleic acids, peptides, proteins, and gene-editing systems.
